I've graded all 27 items (9 per review) and written `verdicts.json`; it parses and has 9 items for each of the three reviews.

| Review | GT-j1 | GT-j2 | GT-j3 | False findings | Unresolved | Non-material |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| blind-106ff2 | — | — | item 3 | 0 | item 5 (NC-1) | 7 |
| blind-154ec8 | item 1 | item 2 | item 4 | 0 | 0 | 6 |
| blind-9acb5e | items 1, 2 | — | item 3 | 0 | 0 | 6 |

Every recovery has fix sufficiency `absent`: no item proposes a corrective change.

**GT-j1.** I counted the items saying an `unknown` middleware context now wipes the established ctx as recovering GT-j1. That is the #5037 mechanism: an unconstrained generic falls back to `unknown`, and the new gate lets it replace the ctx, giving the `{}` error. A tsc check against the head confirmed it: a middleware that only throws turns the resolver's ctx into `{}`, while the old definition keeps it.

**Checks behind the verdicts.** I compiled one scratch file (`clone-work/probe.ts`) against the head sources. I did not have a full merge-base build; for the old behaviour I used a local copy of the merge-base `Overwrite` type instead. It showed:
- Arrays, tuples, `Date` and branded strings were already mangled by the old `Overwrite` in the same way, as were optional and readonly modifiers and union inputs. The items raising those are accurate but describe problems the PR didn't introduce, so they are `non-material`.
- `Overwrite<X, never>` gives `never` both before and after the PR. The dead-branch and doc-comment items are therefore hygiene, as are the test-coverage and design items, which the register lists as non-defects.

**Three judgement calls you may want to recheck:**
- **blind-9acb5e item 2** (a middleware typed `any` erases the ctx). The regression is confirmed at the head, and the old definition keeps the ctx. I assigned it to GT-j1, grouped with item 1, reasoning that the upstream fix (#5039) also restores this case. I worked that out on paper and did not run it, so the assignment could reasonably be argued the other way.
- **NC-1 (blind-106ff2 item 5).** `Overwrite<any, unknown>` changes from an object that allows any property to `unknown`. I confirmed that with tsc, but not the full path through `ResolveOptions` and `MiddlewareFunction`. #5039 wouldn't fix this case, and whether it matters depends on real-world helpers typed against the default `ProcedureParams`, which the reviewer admits the repo doesn't have. It is filed as a new candidate for adjudication.
- **blind-106ff2 item 3.** It also mentions the GT-j1 `unknown` collapse in passing, but its main claim is the nullable ctx override, so I assigned it to GT-j3.
